name: Labrador 0.3.0
body:
The third release of Labrador, a 2D game engine in C++20 for Windows and a desktop browser. It is the first release with its own documentation, frozen at this tag, and the first with a starter ZIP, so Get Started can begin without Git.

**Releases are versioned, and before 1.0 a release promises a record, not compatibility.** A 0.x tag promises one thing about the tag before it: every consumer-visible change between the two is an entry in CHANGES.md, with its migration where it has one.

Every consumer-visible change since `v0.2.0`: [CHANGES.md, v0.3.0](https://github.com/matt439/Labrador/blob/v0.3.0/CHANGES.md#v030-2026-11-03). Moving a game from `v0.2.0` meets two source breaks: the math library moved from `mattmath` to `labrador`, with its target renamed from `MattMath` to `LabradorMath`, and constants are now spelt in snake_case (`Vector2F::ZERO` is now `Vector2F::zero`). [Update your code for a newer Labrador](https://labradorengine.com/docs/guides/migrate/) makes both edits with commands to copy. New public names are not consumer-visible and are not listed there; among those this release adds are a seeded `Random` that gives the same stream on every platform, hiding and confining the pointer, and controller vibration.

`labrador-starter-v0.3.0.zip` is the Get Started project with this release inside it, built without Git: [Get the starter project](https://labradorengine.com/docs/get-started/starter/).

**The settle criterion.** The API settles after twelve weeks and two 0.x tags in which CHANGES.md gains no entry; 1.0 is the first tag cut once both have run. Unmet: CHANGES.md's newest entry is `d98ef3d`, dated 2026-10-29, and no 0.x tag has been cut since it.

**Supported revisions.** The latest tag and `master` are supported; a fix ships as a new tag from `master`, never as a patch to an old tag ([SECURITY.md](https://github.com/matt439/Labrador/blob/v0.3.0/SECURITY.md)).

What a release promises, and how a public name leaves the engine: [PHILOSOPHY, The public face](https://github.com/matt439/Labrador/blob/v0.3.0/docs/design/PHILOSOPHY.md#the-public-face).
